case_title.reason: Title matches the judgment's caption: Charandas Swami v. State of Gujarat & Anr.

number_of_accused.reason: Three appellants (Accused 1, 2, 5) whose liability is decided; Accused 3 did not appeal, so 3 is defensible.

accused_gender.reason: All accused are men; the judgment refers to Accused 3 as 'his' house and similar male references.

accused_age.reason: No accused age is stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: Accused are described as temple functionaries of a sect, but no religion is stated for them individually; 'Not stated' is defensible.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.reason: Judgment describes Accused 1 as Assistant Kothari and others as henchmen/assistants at the temple.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Unexplained high-value cash and investments found at the accused's residences are stated.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned in the judgment.

victim_age.reason: Only 'advanced age' is mentioned; no numeric age is stated.

victim_caste.reason: No caste of the victim is named.

victim_religion.reason: Victim's religion is not stated; sect/temple association alone is not an explicit religious identity statement.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Prosecution case of rivalry over the proposed transfers and fear of exposure is accurately described.

offence_category.reason: Main offence is murder under s.302 r/w s.120-B.

statutory_provisions.reason: Judgment confirms ss.302 r/w 120-B, 364 and 201 IPC, with 201 applying to Accused 2 and 5.

weapon.reason: No weapon was recovered; strangulation is the method, with khesiya only in the panchnama account.

evidence_type.reason: Case rests on circumstantial evidence, disclosures, recovery, medical and DNA identification, and hostile witnesses.

confession.reason: No confession; s.27 disclosures by Accused 3 and 5 were held admissible and relied on.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Body burnt and dumped, car burnt, false insurance claim and misleading conduct are all noted.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating facts are noted; prosecution's non-support of rarest-of-rare is procedural, not mitigation.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Matches the judgment: death under s.302 r/w 120-B, life RI under s.364, and 5 years RI under s.201 for Accused 2 and 5.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court upheld conviction of 1, 2, 3, 5, acquitted 4, and commuted death to life.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeals of Accused 1, 2 and 5, upholding conviction.

offence_finally_established.reason: Convictions under s.302, s.364 r/w 120-B and s.201 for Accused 2 and 5 are consistent with the judgment.

imprisonment_type.reason: Death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment, which the Supreme Court upheld.

imprisonment_years.reason: Final sentence is life, not a fixed term, so null is correct.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is mentioned in the judgment.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Neutral summary of the prosecution case without gendered references to the accused or judicial reasoning about the evidence.
neutral_facts.quote: proposed transferring a senior temple official and his associates
neutral_facts.reason: Uses gendered pronoun 'his' for accused and says 'the court weighed' evidence, which is judicial reasoning rather than evidence presented at trial.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment does not state the statutory maximum or minimum punishment.

attempt_completion.reason: Murder was completed; the victim's death is established.

physical_harm.reason: Death by asphyxia from strangulation, with body later burnt and dumped, matches the judgment.

number_of_offences.correct_value: 4 charged (ss.302, 120-B, 364, 201); 4 sections upheld across appellants: s.302, 120-B, 364 for Accused 1, 2, 5; s.201 for Accused 2 and 5
number_of_offences.quote: Accused Nos. l, 2, 3 and 5 for offences under Sections 302 r/w 120-B, 364 and 201
number_of_offences.reason: Value wrongly limits s.302, 120-B and 364 to Accused 1 and 5; Accused 2 is also convicted of them.

financial_property_loss.reason: Misappropriation and kickbacks are alleged, with amounts not quantified in the judgment.

premeditation_planning.reason: Trial court found pre-planning and the Supreme Court accepted the conspiracy as hatched and executed.

motive.reason: Fear of transfer, loss of control and exposure of financial irregularities is the motive the courts accepted.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Accepted evidence matches the judgment's list of circumstances, including last-seen, body identification, disclosures, call records and car burning.

witness_credibility.reason: Hostile witnesses' admissible parts, PW30, PW32 and medical discrepancies are accurately described.

post_offence_conduct.reason: Body dumping, car burning, false insurance claim and misleading the investigation are accurately listed.

custody_duration.reason: Duration of custody is not stated in the judgment.

bail_history.reason: Judgment states 'The Accused on bail shall surrender forthwith', supporting the value.

trial_duration.reason: Dates for offence (03.05.1998), trial judgment (11.06.2004), HC (01.09.2006) and SC (April 10, 2017) match the judgment.

legal_representation.reason: Huzefa Ahmadi and K.T.S. Tulsi for appellants and Ms. Kiran Suri for respondent are named in the judgment.

investigation_status.reason: Missing complaint, CBI transfer, CBI FIR, arrests, charge sheet and completed trial are all stated.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Investigating authorities were not careful in choosing panchas with prior disputes (held not to make evidence inadmissible); lacunae in investigation noted by High Court.
procedural_irregularity.quote: noticing ee11ain lacunae in the investigation, but the High Court found that the same did not impact the credibility
procedural_irregularity.reason: Omits the High Court's noted investigation lacunae; dropping FIR-named persons was not noted as an irregularity by the court.

appeal_history.reason: Trial, High Court and Supreme Court outcomes, including Accused 3 not appealing, match the judgment.

prosecution_argument.reason: Conspiracy by inference, motive, last-seen, disposal, panchnama, recovery and conduct arguments are accurately listed.

defence_argument.reason: No meeting of minds, imaginary motive, broken last-seen theory, s.27 inadmissibility, and medical/DNA doubts are all argued.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Concurrent findings not disturbed unless perverse; conspiracy by inference; and s.27 limits are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Subbaiah Ambalam (AIR 1977 SC 2046); David Rozario (2002) 7 SCC 728; Baliya (2012) 9 SCC 696; Pulukuri Kottaya (AIR 1947 PC 67); Mohmed Inayatullah (1976) 1 SCC 828; Navjot Sandhu (2005) 11 SCC 600; Vasanta Sampat Dupare (2015) 1 SCC 253; State of Maharashtra v. Damu (2000) 6 SCC 269; Sharad Birdhichand Sarda (1984) 4 SCC 116
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Reliance was also placed on the recent decision of this Court in the case of Dupure (supra).
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Omits Vasanta Sampat Dupare and Damu, which the Supreme Court relied on extensively for s.27 admissibility.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Supreme Court upheld the High Court's sentence without separate sentencing reasoning, so 'Not applicable' fits.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The Supreme Court weighed no mitigating factors for sentence.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The Supreme Court did not weigh aggravating factors for sentence; the heinousness point is the trial court's.

other_sentence_order.reason: Accused on bail were directed to surrender forthwith, as the judgment states.
